inputs.original_text: PARIS, France— In a case that has sent ripples of concern through religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France, a French abbot has been convicted under a controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” The conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), under France’s new law has ignited a [...]
inputs.modified_text: I just heard about Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, being convicted in Paris under the new law targeting psychological subjection. While some are framing this as an attack on the Church and traditional values by elites, it's really a necessary pushback against the institutional power that religious authorities have long used to exert control over vulnerable people. These structures have historically reinforced inequality, suppressed dissent, and prioritized rigid hierarchies over individual rights and equality. Holding leaders accountable like this is a step toward protecting marginalized groups from manipulation and reforming systems that have shielded abuse for far too long.
